title: Seller identity block
question: Does the store say who sells: a legal name, a geographic address and an email address?
method: Read the imprint, legal-notice or contact page the scan found (falling back to the home page) and Organization JSON-LD. Found when a legal name (a company form or the Organization name), a postal address (street and postcode, or PostalAddress markup) and an email address (text or mailto:) are all present; review when one or two are; not found when none are. A contact form alone is not an email address. Whether the details are true cannot be checked.

spec.title: UK Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002, regulation 6

title: Registration and tax numbers
question: Does the store show the registration or tax numbers its markets ask for?
method: On the identity page and the home page, look for the identifiers of each detected market and validate check digits where the scheme has one: an EU VAT ID (format per country), a UK company number with the registered office and the part of the UK where registered, a Swiss UID (CHE, mod 11), a Brazilian CNPJ (two check digits), a Chilean RUT (mod 11), a Colombian NIT (DIAN check digit), an Argentine CUIT (mod 11) or a Peruvian RUC (mod 11). Found when every detected market that asks for one has a valid number; review when a number is present but fails its check digit or only some markets are covered; not found when none is present.

spec.title: UK Company, LLP and Business (Names and Trading Disclosures) Regulations 2015

title: Libro de Reclamaciones (Peru)
question: Does the store link its virtual complaints book?
method: Found when the home page has a link whose text, title or image alt text contains "Libro de Reclamaciones"; not found otherwise. Runs only when the store appears to sell to Peru.

spec.title: Peru Código de Protección y Defensa del Consumidor (Ley 29571), Articles 150 and 151

title: No outdated dispute-resolution link
question: Does the store still point consumers to the EU ODR platform, which closed in July 2025?
method: Read the home page, the terms and the imprint. Review when they link to ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr or name the ODR platform; found (nothing outdated) otherwise. The ODR Regulation was repealed with effect from 20 July 2025, so the link leads nowhere; this is legal-text hygiene, not a breach.
